The problem that you're going to run into is that, as innocent as your intentions may be, this is exactly the kind of information somebody goes after when casting a dragnet for phishing purposes. Knowing these details gets a potential phisher a lot closer to successfully pulling off a socially-engineered hack, and most people who work in a Help Desk role should be trained to be wary of answering them -- both because they come from a complete stranger and because the answers are transmitted in the clear, for anyone else to read.

That's not to say that you have ulterior motives, or that your idea is particularly terrible; just trying to give you some insight into why you might not get as many bites as you had hoped for. I would give you some sufficiently randomized data, myself, but it's been years since I legitimately filled a Help Desk role, and my info is certainly out of date.

You make a very good point, and in this day and age it's something that DOES need to be taught, and considered more. I was vague enough I don't worry much, but far too often security is an after-thought and not a preventative.

Can you provide information regarding specific tools used at your help desk (tracking software, remote control access, project management)?

Service now (Which I hate with the burning of a thousand suns) for tickets, dameware for local remote support, bomgar for offsite / VPN support. Spreadsheets for projects, although this is rare, we usually just use email talking to each other to manage that. Ordering some stuff and putting it in after hours you don't really need to "manage" that, just don't be dumb.

Can you provide strengths and weaknesses of your help desk function?

Weaknesses, users don't have direct access to us, they have to go through out parent co unhelpdesk first. It's great for us though. My phone never rings and I almost never get interrupted when putting whatever back together.

Strengths, speed and knowledge, our team is all generalists, so between the 4 of us there is very little we haven't done before.

Can you provide information regarding upcoming trends for your help desk operation?

Locking things back down, management wanted more freedom then hackers went wild, so we're rolling back a lot of it. users are pissed, don't care we have data to protect. Bringing a lot of stuff back from the cloud, new OS this year too.

Can you provide information regarding statistical data and how that data is used (reporting tools)?

can't unfortunately, parent org does all that and just gives us marching orders in most cases. We don't track users or anything unless we have manager orders that someone might be slacking. Yeah, I've watched a few people fire themselves.

Can you provide how your organization evaluates products?

You must have a full featured trial, and we trial it. after knowing which 3 or 4 products pass out tests, we buy the cheapest one, usually. exceptions for things that want to be cloudy, we pay more if we can do it all in house. A Lot of vendors probably hate us for that.

Can you provide how your organization communicates to computer users regarding the Information Technology function?

Emails that people don't read, but our ass is covered. "Look we told people, we sent 15 emails in a month leading up to change, 5 in the last week, we can't force people to read them. We treat our users like adults. Not reading important email is not our fault.
